source_text: Ἐχομένοις τοίνυν τοῦ σκοποῦ καὶ τὰς γραφὰς πρὸς τὸ βιωφελὲς τῆς παιδαγωγίας ἐκλεγομένοις, ὁποῖόν τινα εἶναι χρὴ παρ᾿ ὅλον τὸν βίον τὸν Χριστιανὸν καλούμενον, κεφαλαιωδῶς ὑπογραπτέον. ἀρκτέον οὖν ἡμῖν ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν αὐτῶν καὶ ὅπως ἁρμόττειν γε χρή. στοχαζομένοις τοίνυν τῆς συμμετρίας τοῦ συντάγματος, ὁποῖόν τινα τῷ ἑαυτοῦ σώματι ἕκαστον ἡμῶν προσφέρεσθαι, μᾶλλον δὲ ὅπως αὐτὸ κατευθύνειν χρή, λεκτέον· ὁπόταν γάρ τις ἀπὸ τῶν ἐκτὸς καὶ αὐτῆς ἔτι τῆς τοῦ σώματος ἀγωγῆς ἐπὶ τὴν διάνοιαν ἀχθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ λόγου τὴν θεωρίαν τῶν κατὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον συμβαινόντων κατὰ φύσιν ἀκριβῶς ἐκμάθῃ, εἴσεται μὴ σπουδάζειν μὲν περὶ τὰ ἐκτός, τό τε ἴδιον τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, τὸ ὄμμα τῆς ψυχῆς, ἐκκαθαίρειν, ἁγνίζειν δὲ καὶ τὴν σάρκα αὐτήν. ὁ γὰρ ἐκείνων καθαρῶς ἀπολυθείς, δι᾿ ὧν ἔτι χοῦς ἐστιν, τί ἂν ἄλλο προὐργιαίτερον ἑαυτοῦ ἔχοι πρὸς τὸ ὁδῷ ἐλθεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν κατάληψιν τοῦ θεοῦ; οἱ μὲν δὴ ἄλλοι ἄνθρωποι ζῶσιν, ἵνα ἐσθίωσιν, ὥσπερ ἀμέλει καὶ τὰ· ἄλογα ζῷα, οἷς οὐδὲν ἀλλ᾿ ἢ γαστήρ ἐστιν ὁ βίος, ἡμῖν δὲ ὁ παιδαγωγὸς ἐσθίειν παραγγέλλει, ἵνα ζῶμεν. οὔτε γὰρ ἔργον ἡμῖν ἡ τροφὴ οὔτε σκοπὸς ἡδονή, ὑπὲρ δὲ τῆς ἐνταῦθα διαμονῆς, ἣν ὁ λόγος εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν παιδαγωγεῖ, ἐγκρίνεται ἡ τροφή. ἁπλῆ δὲ αὕτη καὶ ἀπερίεργος, ἀληθείᾳ κατάλληλος, ἁπλοῖς καὶ ἀπεριέργοις ἁρμόζουσα παιδίοις, ὡσὰν εἰς τὸ ζῆν, οὐκ εἰς τρυφὴν ἐπιτήδειος· τὸ δὲ ἐκ δυεῖν, τὸ ζῆν τοῦτο, ὑγείας τε καὶ ἰσχύος σύγκειται, οἷς μάλιστα κατάλληλον τῆς τροφῆς τὸ εὔκολον, εἴς τε τὰς ἀναδόσεις καὶ τοῦ σώματος τὴν κουφότητα χρησιμεῦον, ἐξ ὧν αὔξησίς τε καὶ ὑγεία καὶ ἰσχὺς δικαία, οὐχὶ δὲ ἄδικος ἢ σφαλερὰ καὶ ἀθλία ὡς ἡ τῶν ἀθλητῶν ἐξ ἀναγκοφαγίας, περιγίνεται. αἱ μὲν οὖν πολυειδεῖς ποιότητες ἀποπτυστέαι, ποικίλας ἐντίκτουσαι βλάβας, καχεξίας σωμάτων, ἀνατροπὰς στομάχων, ἐκπορνευούσης τῆς γεύσεως διά τινος κακοδαίμονος τέχνης τῆς ὀψαρτυτικῆς καὶ τῆς ἀμφὶ τὰ πέμματα ματαιοτεχνίας. τροφὴν γὰρ τολμῶσιν καλεῖν τὴν ἐν τρυφαῖς ἐπιτήδευσιν εἰς ἡδονὰς ἐπιβλαβεῖς ὀλισθαίνουσαν. Ἀντιφάνης δὲ ὁ Δήλιος ἰατρὸς καὶ μίαν τῶν νόσου αἰτιῶν ταύτην εἴρηκεν τῶν ἐδεσμάτων τὴν πολυειδίαν, τῶν περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν δυσαρεστούντων κενοδοξίᾳ ποικίλῃ τὸ σῶφρον τῆς διαίτης ἐξομνυμένων καὶ τὰς διαποντίους πολυπραγμονούντων ἐδωδάς.
pass_a_gloss: Having therefore the goal and the writings being chosen for the benefit of the education, what kind of person one ought to be throughout the whole life called Christian, we must outline in summary. It is enough for us to start from ourselves and how we must harmonize. To those therefore who are considering the symmetry of the constitution, what kind of person each of us is offering to his own body, rather what kind of person we must guide it, must be said; for when someone is led by the word from the outside things and even from the guidance of the body to the mind, and he learns accurately the theory of the things happening to man according to nature, he will know not to be eager about the outside things, but to cleanse the eye of the soul, which is the person's own, and to purify also the flesh itself. For the one who is purely freed from the things through which he is still earth, what other thing would he have more useful for himself to come on the way to the comprehension of God? Other people live to eat, just like also the irrational animals, for which life is nothing but the stomach, but to us the educator commands to eat so that we may live. For neither is food our work nor is pleasure our goal, but rather the food is judged for the stay here, which the word educates to immortality. And this food is simple and not elaborate, suitable for the truth, harmonizing with simple and not elaborate children, as if for living, not for luxury; and the living, which is from two things, consists of health and strength, for which the easy food is especially suitable, being useful for the evacuations and the lightness of the body, from which comes the growth and the health and the just strength, not the unjust or dangerous and miserable one, as that of the athletes from forced eating. The many-colored qualities must therefore be spit out, introducing various damages, bad conditions of bodies, upsets of stomachs, from the taste being corrupted by some evil demon's technique of cooking and the useless skill concerning the foods. For they dare to call food the indulgence in luxuries, slipping into harmful pleasures. But Antiphanes the Delian doctor has said that one of the causes of disease is this variety of foods, of those who are displeased with the truth, boasting with various vanity, swearing falsely to the sane diet, and being busy with the crossing foods.
pass_b_english: Therefore, keeping the goal in view and selecting the Scriptures for the benefit of our education, we must outline in summary what kind of person the one called a Christian ought to be throughout his entire life. We must begin with ourselves and with how we ought to harmonize our lives. Accordingly, as we consider the symmetry of our constitution — what each of us presents to his own body, or rather how we ought to guide it — we must say this: when someone is led by the Word from external things, and even from the discipline of the body, to the mind, and he accurately learns the theory of the things that happen to a human being according to nature, he will understand that he must not be eager about external things, but must cleanse the eye of the soul, which is his own, and purify the flesh itself as well. For the one who has been purely freed from the things through which he is still earth, what could he have that is more useful for himself to advance on the way toward the comprehension of God? Other people live to eat, just like irrational animals, for whom life is nothing but the stomach; but our Educator commands us to eat so that we may live. For food is not our work, nor is pleasure our goal; rather, food is judged necessary for our stay here, which the Word educates toward immortality. And this food is simple and unelaborate, suited to the truth, harmonizing with simple and unelaborate children, as it were, fit for living, not for luxury. And this living, which consists of two things — health and strength — is best served by simple food, which is useful for the evacuations and the lightness of the body, from which come growth, health, and just strength, not unjust or precarious and miserable strength like that of athletes from forced eating. Therefore the many-colored qualities of food must be spat out, since they introduce various harms, bad conditions of bodies, upsets of stomachs, the taste being corrupted by some evil demon's technique of cooking and the useless skill concerning delicacies. For they dare to call food the indulgence in luxuries, which slips into harmful pleasures. But Antiphanes the Delian physician has said that one of the causes of disease is this variety of foods, practiced by those who are displeased with the truth, who boast in various vanity, who swear falsely against the temperate diet, and who busy themselves with exotic foods from across the sea.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex syntax of the section regarding the 'eye of the soul' and the comparison to athletes. The translation of 'διὰ τινος κακοδαίμονος τέχνης τῆς ὀψαρτυτικῆς' as 'by some evil demon's technique of cooking' (Pass A) and 'by some evil demon's technique of cooking' (Pass B) is faithful to the Greek. The identification of 'διὰ πόντους' (implied by 'διὰ πόντους' or similar context in 'διὰ πόντους/πολυπραγμονούντων' - though the Greek text provided says 'διὰ πόντους' is not explicitly there, it uses 'διὰ πόντους' in some manuscripts, but here it says 'διὰ πόντους' is not in the provided Greek; however, Pass B translates 'διὰ πόντους' as 'from across the sea' which is a standard interpretation of 'διὰ πόντους' if it were present, but looking at the provided Greek: 'τὰς διαποντίους πολυπραγμονούντων ἐδωδάς'. Pass B translates this as 'exotic foods from across the sea', which is a correct rendering of 'διαποντίους'.)
